clue.text: Be experienced, but in less than three subjects?

definitions.meaning: a playful literal reading: knowing just one or two matters

explanation.surface: A jibe that someone's experience is very narrow, limited to a couple of topics.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be shrewd and well informed through experience; read literally it means knowledge of only one or two items.

clue.text: How neck brace gives one confidence?

definitions.text: How neck brace gives one confidence?

parts.words: How neck brace gives one confidence?
parts.note: a neck brace literally holds the head high, which is also the idiom for staying cheerful in adversity

explanation.surface: A question about how a surgical collar might boost morale.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means staying brave and cheerful, while a brace literally props the jaw upward.

clue.text: I do believe daggers are concealed

indicators.note: the plural word is tucked away inside the run of letters across 'I do believe'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that weapons have been hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger-shaped printing mark, and its plural names several such marks.

clue.text: Charles de Gaulle, for example, had dry wine

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: The French general apparently drank a dry wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle is the main international hub serving Paris, an example of a terminal for flights.

clue.text: Gaunt-looking witch given rough pull-up

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to drag something is to haul it roughly

explanation.surface: A witch looks gaunt after a hard workout of pull-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard describes a worn, hollow-cheeked, exhausted appearance, a synonym for gaunt.

clue.text: Incisions carved on chest

indicators.note: carving reshapes material, so the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cuts made into someone's chest, or a wooden chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Notches are small V-shaped cuts, which are incisions.

clue.text: Pulling hard together, they may have a stroke

definitions.text: Pulling hard together, they may have a stroke

parts.words: Pulling hard together, they may have a stroke
parts.note: sounds like overexerted people risking a medical stroke, but describes a rowing crew pulling in time and following their stroke, the rower who sets the rhythm

explanation.surface: Strenuous group effort could bring on a medical emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew pulls together, and its stroke is the crew member setting the pace.

clue.text: Stuart and Ken forced to share

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Two men named Stuart and Ken are made to share something.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is to share a task or object by alternating, so it means share.

clue.text: Comment on letters from look-out site

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an observation is a remark or comment
post is the mail, the letters delivered

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on correspondence sent from a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a military position for watching the enemy, a lookout site.

clue.text: Look properly round British plant

indicators.note: the two words go round the abbreviation, holding it between them

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
right as an adverb means correctly or properly

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine a British plant carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used to treat eye complaints, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Tends the lawn slopes

definitions.meaning: clears grass of leaves and moss with a garden tool
inclines, as a ship's mast or a stage leans at an angle

explanation.surface: A gardener working on a lawn that is on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener rakes leaves off grass, and a rake is also an angle of inclination, so the verb means slopes.

clue.text: Journey to Australia with a philosopher

parts.note: a spin is a short trip or drive
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker takes a trip down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a 17th-century Dutch rationalist philosopher.

clue.text: Pet's speed round mile run

indicators.note: the speed word goes round the abbreviation for mile

parts.note: haste means speed or hurry
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A pet races around a mile-long run.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Pet' with 's standing for 'is' to link it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent kept as a household pet, an example of the category.

clue.text: Herb in French street

definitions.meaning: a bitter aromatic plant used in medicine
the French word for a street

explanation.surface: A herb found on a street in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a strong-smelling herb, and in French it is the word for street.

clue.text: Denied information got back to a 50s hooligan

indicators.note: reading backwards, the information word is turned round

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth with Edwardian dress, often seen as a troublemaker

explanation.surface: A 1950s tearaway was refused information he had returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny or nullify it, so negated means denied.

clue.text: One's final word, as one's retiring

definitions.text: One's final word, as one's retiring

parts.words: One's final word, as one's retiring
parts.note: sounds like last words before death or departure, but means the farewell said when going to bed

explanation.surface: Someone utters a last remark on leaving their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The farewell said before going to bed is the last thing one says on retiring for the night.

clue.text: Not quite — even for woman

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is lost

explanation.surface: A remark that something is not quite fair for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, stands in crosswords for a woman.

clue.text: Sound more annoyed, after second punch from Spaniard

indicators.note: the sound-alike comes after the single letter
sound tells us to go by how the comparative word is said, not spelt

parts.note: angrier means more annoyed

explanation.surface: A Spaniard sounds angrier after being punched a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a blow, but it is the drink. In non-rhotic British speech, 'angrier' is said like ANGRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch with fruit, so it is a punch from a Spaniard.

clue.text: Nothing is beneath notice — such a fuss

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means this piece comes below the other

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
O, the round figure, represents nothing

explanation.surface: Something too trivial to notice causing a great fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means bustle or trouble, a synonym for fuss.

clue.text: Liverpudlian firm introduced to dollar customer

indicators.note: the firm is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: S stands for the dollar sign
a user is a customer of a service
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A Liverpool business offering dollar deals to its clients.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouser is the informal British name for someone from Liverpool.

clue.text: For fans, amazing crocus

indicators.note: amazing hints at a maze, the letters thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A stunning crocus to delight its admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is the spice from the autumn crocus, and also names that crocus itself.

clue.text: Run with friends to mass meetings

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
allies are friends or partners

explanation.surface: Someone hurries with companions to big gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallies are large public gatherings held to support a cause, mass meetings.

clue.text: Clipped coin encompassed ruin for magnates

indicators.note: the shortened coin word goes round the ruin word
a clipped coin has its edge shaved, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: loss means ruin or deprivation

explanation.surface: Clipping coins brought financial ruin to rich tycoons.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are giants, figuratively great figures, so magnates as titans of industry.

clue.text: American city was elegant in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
ago means at a past time

explanation.surface: A US city that used to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major city in Illinois, USA.

clue.text: The French porter has to stay to the end

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
stout is a dark beer, a strong porter

explanation.surface: A French hotel porter must remain until closing.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure or survive until the finish, so to stay to the end.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tree whose timber is a wood used for tool handles.

clue.text: All one can take — more than one can manage

definitions.meaning: the amount a hand can hold
a troublesome person, as a naughty child is a real problem to control

explanation.surface: Someone at their limit, overwhelmed by too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful is the quantity a hand can grasp, and also a person hard to control.

clue.text: Cut short rude remark, given popular medical treatment

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an insult is a rude remark
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A doctor interrupting an insult before handing out a well-liked therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone given by injection to treat diabetes, a medical treatment.

clue.text: Discover there's money to make

parts.note: L stands for pound (libra), money
to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Finding out there is cash to be made.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn a fact is to find it out, so learn means discover.

clue.text: African country takes most of another

indicators.note: most of the word means it loses its final letters

parts.note: the clue's other African country here is its large southern neighbour Nigeria

explanation.surface: One African nation annexes most of its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another African country, the neighbouring Nigeria with its last two letters dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Lover moving to Romania

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart relocating to Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover, from the Italian for one enamoured.

clue.text: Make a mistake, as one may with a shoe

definitions.meaning: commit a blunder or a tactless gaffe

definitions.text: as one may with a shoe
definitions.meaning: literally insert a foot into a shoe when putting it on

explanation.surface: Getting dressed and blundering at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means saying something tactless; literally, one inserts a foot into a shoe.
